record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: global minimality of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution
record.original_question: In the same unit-disc Ginzburg-Landau problem with boundary value g(x)=x, let E_epsilon(u) = (1/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 + (1/(4 epsilon^2)) integral_Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on the class H^1_g(Omega; R^2). Is the radial solution U_epsilon a global minimizer of E_epsilon on H^1_g(Omega; R^2) for every epsilon > 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.2. Is U_epsilon a minimizer of E_epsilon on H^1_g(Omega; R^2) for any epsilon > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disc, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be the boundary map $g(x) = x$. For $\varepsilon > 0$ define the Ginzburg–Landau energy
\[ E_\varepsilon(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + \tfrac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2\,dx \]
on the affine Sobolev space
\[ H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) : u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}. \]
By symmetrization, there exists a unique radial critical point $U_\varepsilon(x) = f_\varepsilon(|x|)\, x/|x|$, where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ solves the associated ODE with $f_\varepsilon(0)=0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1)=1$.

Question: Is $U_\varepsilon$ a global minimizer of $E_\varepsilon$ on $H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The two-dimensional case is known in two regimes: for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ the radial degree-one vortex $U_\varepsilon$ is the unique global minimizer (Pacard–Rivière and related works), and for $\varepsilon$ large enough (specifically when $E_\varepsilon$ becomes strictly convex on the admissible set) global minimality also holds. However, for intermediate values of $\varepsilon$ in the unit disc with boundary data $g(x)=x$, the question is reported in recent literature as still open; full global minimality for every $\varepsilon>0$ has been established only in dimensions $N\geq 7$ (Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu).

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of degree-one Ginzburg-Landau vortex in the unit ball
status_evidence.snippet: For any ε > (W'(1)/λ₁)^(1/2), E_ε is strictly convex... has a unique critical point that is the global minimizer. In dimensions N≥7, the radial vortex is the unique global minimizer for all ε>0.
status_evidence.claim: Global minimality of the radial solution in dimension 2 is established only for small or sufficiently large ε; the full range remains open in N=2 while it is settled for N≥7.

status_evidence.title: Vortex sheet solutions for the Ginzburg–Landau system in cylinders: symmetry and global minimality
status_evidence.snippet: The case ε < ε_N is still not solved as stated in Open Problem 2... raised in dimension N=2 for the disk in the book of Bethuel, Brezis and Hélein.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of global minimality for the radial Ginzburg–Landau solution on the unit disc with boundary x is acknowledged as an open problem in subsequent literature.
